sessions.lever: ALLOCDBG priority arithmetic: statement order, schedule placement, param-vs-carrier substitution, split-init accumulation, pointer-operand cast
sessions.note: SIX levers, each measured and each holding 132/132 insns. (1) initialise `i` BEFORE `tbl` - target emits the s4 init pair before the s5 pair, identical registers, different emission order: 23->19. (2) `tbl++` AFTER the first func_8004A348 call rather than mid-buffer - sched1 runs before register allocation in this toolchain, so schedule changes feed allocno live lengths: 19->17. (3) loop2's func_800523E0 takes the PARAMETER a4 instead of the local carrier, dropping the carrier allocno from nrefs 7 to 5 (pri 1473 -> 1052) so out2 (1333) outranks it - this fixes the s6/s7 pair and makes ALL of loop 1 match instruction for instruction: 17->11. (4) loop2 stptr as its own local PLUS split-init on the loop1 stptr (`stptr = base; stptr += 0xFC;`), which raises stptr's nrefs 5 -> 7 (pri 2439 -> 3414) without changing a single emitted instruction and lets the loop2 split keep s3/s4 in target's order: 11->6. (5) `(s32)` cast on the first add's pointer operand: 6->5. ALL EIGHT callee-saved registers now match target. RESIDUAL IS FIVE INSTRUCTIONS, one cluster in loop 2: target gives loop 2 its own a4+0x20 allocno in s3 (sharing with the dead loop1 stptr) where we reuse loop1's s6, and the parameter substitution costs `lw a0,88(sp)` where target has `move a0,s7`. KEY TOOL: tmp/allocone.sh isolates the function into its own TU, so the ALLOCDBG table needs no block-alignment guesswork (allocno numbering, nrefs, livelen and pri are all per-function). src/text1a.c reverted to HEAD.

root_cause: Pure register allocation. GCC 2.7.2 orders allocnos by pri = floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs/livelen*10000 and hands each the lowest-numbered non-conflicting callee-saved register, so every register difference reduces to an inequality between two allocno priorities. All eight are now in target's order; the last five instructions need a per-loop `a4+0x20` allocno whose priority lands in (1052,1666), which needs a +1 reference lever - every lever found so far moves +2 (split-init) or 0 (aliasing).

Restore `move a0,s7` at loop2's func_800523E0 by holding the carrier's priority below out2's 1333 some way other than the parameter substitution (which costs the stack reload).
